Risk: EMR or PAS cannot support modern SSO (SAML/OIDC), needing a custom connector
Mitigation: Confirm protocol support for every in-scope app during the current-state assessment (1.2.1); make vendor-confirmed connectors a mandatory RFQ criterion
Contingency: Front the app with an application proxy or password-vaulting SSO and move it to wave 3
Trigger: App vendor cannot confirm SAML/OIDC support by Gate 2

Risk: Inaccurate HR data (job codes, managers, end dates) grants wrong access or removes access in error
Mitigation: HR data cleansing before 1.3.2; run leaver automation in report-only mode for two weeks with daily reconciliation
Contingency: Switch affected changes to a manual approval queue; restore wrongly removed clinical access through the break-glass process within 15 minutes

Risk: Clinicians resist MFA at shared ward workstations and adopt workarounds
Mitigation: Tap-and-go FIDO2 security keys for shared workstations; clinical champions at every site; nurses in UAT
Contingency: Extend that site's rollout by one week with floor-walkers and extra keys
Trigger: Site MFA enrolment below 80% two weeks after rollout

Risk: Implementation partner loses or reassigns a key integration engineer
Mitigation: Named-resource clause with 10-day replacement and service credits; configuration documented in GitHub
Contingency: Call on the standing-offer second partner; resequence SSO waves to protect the critical path
Trigger: Key engineer absent for more than 5 working days

Risk: Platform procurement and contract negotiation run late, delaying design
Mitigation: Issue the RFQ in week 3 with a pre-approved contract template; legal engaged from kickoff
Contingency: Start role model and test strategy early and use the vendor's trial tenant for design
Trigger: Contract not signed by the M3 date

Risk: Licence prices rise (USD-priced quote or exchange rate) before contract signature
Mitigation: Require AUD-denominated pricing held for 90 days in the RFQ
Contingency: Draw on contingency; license lower-risk contractor identities on a cheaper tier
Trigger: Final quote exceeds the baseline licence line by more than 5%

Risk: Clinical staff unavailable for UAT because of roster pressure
Mitigation: Book testers six weeks ahead with funded backfill shifts; agree dates with the Director of Nursing
Contingency: Add evening UAT sessions and test critical clinical scenarios first; if UAT still slips, shorten the pilot from 10 to 7 days with sponsor approval
Trigger: Fewer than 70% of booked testers attend in UAT week 1

Risk: Misconfigured conditional access policy locks users or administrators out
Mitigation: Two monitored break-glass accounts excluded from policies; policies run in report-only mode first; every policy change peer-reviewed through change control
Contingency: Invoke the rollback runbook and break-glass access; communicate through the service desk
Trigger: More than 20 lockouts in one hour

Risk: Credential phishing attack succeeds during the transition while old and new sign-ins coexist
Mitigation: MFA for remote access and admin accounts in wave 1; sign-in risk alerts monitored daily
Contingency: Run the cyber incident response plan; assess for a notifiable data breach to the OAIC
Trigger: Risky sign-in alert or user report of a suspicious prompt

Risk: Departments push extra applications into phase 1 (scope creep)
Mitigation: Signed scope statement with a named out-of-scope list; all requests through the change control board
Contingency: CCB defers new apps to the phase 2 backlog; contingency used only with sponsor approval
Trigger: More than two change requests for new apps in a month

Risk: Identity or audit data stored offshore conflicts with privacy obligations
Mitigation: Australian data residency as a mandatory RFQ criterion; privacy impact assessment (1.2.3) before contract
Contingency: Select the vendor's Australian region or the runner-up vendor
Trigger: PIA identifies offshore storage of personal information

Risk: Project manager or a workstream lead unavailable for an extended period
Mitigation: Named deputy for each role; decisions and plans kept in GitHub and Jira
Contingency: Deputy steps in; re-baseline the schedule through change control if needed
